label: HPE OfficeConnect 1420 5G PoE+ 32W (JH328A)
description: 5-port gigabit PoE+ unmanaged switch: 5x 1G, 4x PoE+, 32 W PoE budget, no console.

poe.note: HPE's own figure, not the model name. The 1420 QuickSpecs (v10, 2019) JH328A page prints "This product provides PoE or PoE+ power across 4 of 5 ports, with a total power budget of 32W", and the series' power-consumption table in the switch's own guide prints "Total PoE output 32 W" with "Max. PoE power per port 30 W" and "Max. PoE ports at full 30 W output: 1". So the 32 W is a PSE allocation and it buys one 30 W device, not four: 32 W across four PoE+ ports is 8 W each on average. Maximum power rating 40 W including the whole PoE output, 5 W without it.

notes: Vendor figures for **JH328A**: 5 gigabit ports, **PoE+ (802.3at) on 4 of them**, total budget **32 W**. **32 W across four PoE+ ports is 8 W each** - it will run four phones or two 802.3at access points, and it will not run four 30 W devices no matter what the port count suggests.
